promises.promise: Permission from a person for an agent to do one specific thing. An approval covers one of four things: a merge, running a command on a machine, changing a setting, or another dangerous action.
Shows each request with what happens if you allow it and if you deny it.
Lets a person allow or deny, with the exact change in front of them.
Shows a card inline in chat when a setting change or a dangerous action is asked for there.
Holds standing rules, and keeps a permanent record of every request, answer and use.
A merge approval names a pull request at one exact commit.
The agent asking, the project it concerns, and a member when it is private.
An approval records the conversation it was asked in.
A pending approval is an item in a person's Inbox, with a link back here.
Work that waits on an approval is a trigger that fires once, when it is answered.
An agent files what it wants to do, to exactly what, and why. An allowance lasts a set number of minutes and is spent once. A request can also be denied, withdrawn or expire.

A rule answers one kind of request the same way every time, for a scope such as certain repositories or commands. A rule that names a person is a grant to that person. Only the household owner edits rules.

When a person asks an agent in chat to change a setting or do something dangerous, the agent proposes it. Loom shows an approval card inline, with exactly what will change, before and after. On Allow loom makes the change itself and records it. Ordinary work needs no card.

Revoking a token, revoking a machine and signing out a browser cannot be put back. An agent proposes one the same way as a settings change. Allowing it takes a second, explicit yes. Denying it takes one answer.
Loom keeps every request, answer and use in a record that is never edited. Steps an agent took under a tell-me-after rule are listed as reported steps.

An open household approval card can show an advisory caution based on the proposal checks. Allow always checks again and can refuse for additional reasons. For example, Tempo can refuse a repeating schedule for today when its last scheduled time has passed. The caution can be up to 60 seconds stale while the card stays open. It refreshes on focus, on the timer, and after a refused Allow. Both answer buttons stay available.
a Three labels. An approval carries the agent asking, the project it concerns, and a member when it is private to them.

b Who sees it. A household owner sees everything, including what is private to another member. Anyone else sees approvals in their projects and approvals of agents they own. Private to a member means that member plus household owners.
c Checked at the door. Loom applies this to callers from outside: a person, an agent, a machine, someone's own program. Loom's own parts read without asking.
The pending request shows its question, reason, outcomes and exact target.
The request offers Allow and Deny.
The request shows its permanent request record.
